skill.name: mastra
skill.description: Guides AI assistants through current Mastra framework documentation, setup, API verification, troubleshooting, and migration workflows for TypeScript agent projects.
skill.summary: Build and troubleshoot Mastra agents using current local or remote documentation.
skill.author: mastra-ai

security_audit.summary: Static findings are almost entirely documentation examples, Markdown formatting, official documentation URLs, localhost references, or placeholder environment variable usage. I found no prompt injection or hidden execution logic, but the setup guide does encourage users to provide an API key to the AI agent, which is a real secret-handling risk.

remediation.issue: The automatic setup flow asks users to give the AI agent an API key.
remediation.suggestion: Replace this with instructions to use placeholders in generated files and have users add real keys directly to their local .env file or secret manager.

remediation.issue: Example credentials include a concrete local database password.
remediation.suggestion: Use placeholder values and label any local-only examples clearly so users do not copy weak credentials into shared environments.

remediation.issue: Several setup and migration commands are presented for agent workflows.
remediation.suggestion: State that commands should be reviewed before execution and that package installation or migration commands require user approval.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Disclosure Encouraged During Automatic Setup
semantic_findings.description: The setup guide offers an automatic setup option where the user gives the AI agent an API key. This can encourage users to paste real provider credentials into chat instead of storing them locally.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The wording explicitly asks for an API key for automatic setup, and later instructs creating a .env file with provider keys. This is a clear secret-handling risk, although there is no evidence of exfiltration code.

content.user_title: Build Mastra Agents with Current Docs
content.value_statement: Mastra APIs change quickly, so older examples can create broken agents and workflows. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to verify current docs before writing code.
actual_capabilities: Directs assistants to embedded Mastra docs in installed node_modules packages.
Explains CLI and manual setup paths for new Mastra projects.
Documents required TypeScript module settings and provider model format.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for agents, workflows, memory, storage, and environment variables.
Outlines remote documentation lookup using mastra.ai llms.txt and markdown URLs.
Supports migration planning with current API verification steps.
limitations: It does not install packages or run commands by itself.
Remote documentation can be newer than the installed package version.
Examples use placeholder credentials and simple demo agents.
It assumes a TypeScript and Node.js project environment.

use_cases.title: Create a Mastra project
use_cases.description: Set up a new agent project with the right dependencies, TypeScript settings, and provider model format.

use_cases.title: Fix framework errors
use_cases.description: Diagnose common Mastra errors by checking local docs, current type definitions, and known troubleshooting patterns.

use_cases.title: Plan a version upgrade
use_cases.description: Compare current and target APIs, find migration guidance, and build a validation checklist before changing code.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Mastra skill to help me create a new Mastra project. Ask before running commands and use placeholders for secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Verify an API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use embedded Mastra docs to verify the Agent constructor for my installed version before changing my code.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot an error
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the common errors reference and current docs to diagnose this Mastra error: [paste error]. Explain the likely cause and fix.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the migration guide, embedded docs, and remote docs to plan a Mastra version upgrade. List breaking changes and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Help me start a Mastra project for a support agent.
output: The skill checks whether Mastra packages are installed.
It recommends a CLI or manual setup path.
It keeps provider keys as local placeholders.

output_examples.input: My workflow fails after the first step.
output: The skill compares the error with common workflow issues.
It verifies current workflow APIs from installed docs.
It suggests a focused fix and a test step.

output_examples.input: Upgrade my Mastra project to the latest version.
output: The skill starts with official migration guidance.
It checks installed package docs for exact signatures.
It produces a migration plan with validation steps.

best_practices: Check embedded docs first when Mastra packages are installed.
Keep provider keys in local environment files or a secret manager.
Validate TypeScript settings and package versions before debugging APIs.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on model memory for Mastra API signatures.
Do not paste real API keys into chat for project setup.
Do not mix remote docs with older installed packages without checking versions.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants build, debug, and migrate Mastra TypeScript agent projects using current documentation.

faq.question: Why does it prefer embedded docs?
faq.answer: Embedded docs match the installed package version, so they reduce errors from outdated examples.

faq.question: Can it create a full Mastra project?
faq.answer: It can guide project creation and file structure, but command execution should remain user approved.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Should I provide real API keys to the assistant?
faq.answer: No. Use placeholders in generated files, then add real keys locally or through a secret manager.

faq.question: When should remote docs be used?
faq.answer: Use remote docs when local packages are missing or when you need current conceptual guidance.
